correctness.rationale: All possible radius-r balls satisfy four triple-nonnegativity inequalities, one complete path inequality (normal squared norm 22), and one complete clique inequality (normal squared norm 10), forcing r<=3/(4+sqrt(22)+sqrt(10)). Exact source-facet enumeration, integer DAG consistency checks, and rational interval certificates for each other facet certify a symmetric center achieving equality, with strict positive margins. Equality fixes all four triple values and one pair sum, and strict slack at the symmetric center shows the optimal-center polytope is five-dimensional.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial bounded-indegree characteristic-imset polytope is a natural 10D Bayesian-network score-equivalence geometry. The exact insphere value, only six of 94 facets touching the symmetric optimal ball, and a full five-dimensional family of optimal centers provide a motivated metric classification not supplied by the existing facet census; not merely new names for already recorded f-vector data.
